title: Histology transformer distinguishes recorded glioma marker labels
summary: ViT-WSI used whole-slide histology to classify recorded IDH1 status in pooled institutional and TCGA glioma data, reporting a patient-level ROC area of0.960. The labels included clinical immunohistochemistry and sequencing references. This is retrospective label-discrimination evidence, not a new mutation discovery or replacement for molecular testing.
ai_technology: Vision transformer; weakly supervised multiple-instance learning
organization: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology; Harbin Medical University

source_review.scope: Actual relevant primary computational/clinical Methods, model/result context and limitations read; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: Pretrained patch embeddings and a learned attention aggregator produce slide representations, fine-tuned for recorded marker-label classification and aggregated across a patient’s slides.
evidence.tested: The wider institutional dataset had5216 slides from1211 patients, with biomarker-defined subsets pooled with TCGA glioma slides for marker modeling. Methods explicitly keep patients distinct across splits; reported IDH1 AUC is patient-aggregated.
evidence.unknown: TCGA was pooled rather than reserved as a wholly untouched external test. Molecular predictors were initialized from a subtype model, whose overlap with downstream test cases was not independently reconciled. The paper describes both ten random70:30 splits and tenfold evaluation; tuning containment is incomplete. Immunostaining proxies and direct sequencing are heterogeneous references. No causal genotype mechanism, real clinical benefit or independent replication is established.
